NotAcceptable.description: A stream was asked of a route that doesn't stream.

Unavailable.description: Try again later (`Retry-After`): too many pending writes (`overloaded`), a `fold-min-epoch` not reached in time (`epoch-not-reached`), or the store failing (`unavailable`).

Problem.description:
An error response: an HTTP status plus a machine-readable `type`.

`type` is a stable identifier clients can branch on; `title` is a
short human summary of that type; `detail` explains this occurrence.
Refusals carry `at`, the source or view that refused.

at.description: For `rejected`: the source or view that refused.

index.description: For `/_tx`: the index of the operation at fault.

Removed.description: Whether a delete found something to remove.

get.description: Server-Sent Events. Each query parameter names a resource that streams and carries, URL-encoded, the query its own stream would take: `?messages=order%3Ddesc%26limit%3D50&total=`. Events are `<resource>.snapshot` and `<resource>.change`, with the data of the resource's own stream; each `id` lists every resource's epoch, dot-separated in request order, for `Last-Event-ID`. At most 32 resources. Browsers allow six HTTP/1.1 connections per host, and every open stream holds one: follow many resources here, not one stream each.
get.summary: Follow several resources on one connection

post.description: All or nothing: one epoch, and any refusal or malformed operation applies none of them (a malformed one is named by `index`). Each operation sees the ones before it. At most 1000 operations.
